metric_definitions.vehicle_population: SMART generated type0 rows. Pedestrians1 and cyclists2 are excluded from all seven vehicle metrics. No generated GT-validity/FOV/offroad deletion is applied. Optional initial_valid is supported by the evaluator, but current InitDiffusion SMART._rollouts output does not emit this field.
metric_definitions.invalid_size_policy: mask is used in input/training handling of invalid log-size annotations, not as an inference-time generated-size filter. Baseline uses linear size; get_output forwards predicted shape with exact fixed ego shape overrides. The current initial-scene path emits no initial_valid and does not mask generated shapes.
metric_definitions.collision_population: All retained generated vehicles, including offroad vehicles and ego if type0; no onroad subset restriction. One snapshot, not a trajectory collision metric or a pair count.
metric_definitions.collision_geometry: Five circle centers along each oriented vehicle length, with center extent from -length/2+width/2 to length/2-width/2. Count a vehicle once if any of the25 circle pair distances to another vehicle is strictly <(width_j+width_k)/sqrt(3.8).
metric_definitions.collision_aggregation: Sum integer vehicle counts involved in >=1 overlap across scenes / sum vehicle counts *100percent. A pair normally contributes two vehicles. This is not the mean of scene-level rates.
metric_definitions.onroad: Vehicle centroid minimum Euclidean distance to all points of compact official centerlines resampled to100points is <=1.5m. This is not a drivable-polygon or vehicle-footprint criterion.
metric_definitions.lat: Only onroad vehicles. Minimum Euclidean distance to resampled centerline points in metres, unsigned; not exact perpendicular distance to continuous segments. Normalize its histogram by the onroad feature count.
metric_definitions.angle: Only onroad vehicles. Vehicle heading minus heading of the segment immediately preceding the nearest centerline point (nearest index clamped to1..last), wrapped with atan2(sinDelta,cosDelta), converted to degrees; histogram uses5degree bins.
metric_definitions.lat_angle_denominator_warning: Offroad vehicles are excluded from lat/angle histograms but remain in L/W/speed/collision. A lower lat JSD alone does not establish more onroad coverage. Report generated_onroad_fraction separately.
metric_definitions.nearest_distance: All vehicle centroids in scenes with>1vehicles, excluding self; singleton scenes contribute no value. Includes ego as candidate and as neighbor.
metric_definitions.attributes: Length,width,speed use all retained generated vehicle rows irrespective of onroad status. Speed is instantaneous velocity norm, not finite-difference trajectory speed.
metric_definitions.ego_inclusion: No metric exclusion for ego. Fixed GT position,heading,shape,type of vehicle ego contribute to nearest/shape/speed/collision and lat/angle when onroad. Ego speed remains generated because fix_ego_velocity=false. Fixed ego pose contributes GT-conditioned mass, so aggregate JSD is not a non-ego-only generation score.
metric_definitions.ego_attribution_limit: These aggregated histograms do not expose ego-specific counts or histograms. Do not assign a particular shape peak wholly to ego or claim an exact4096ego histogram count without an additional per-scene ego decomposition.
metric_definitions.GT_population: Cached GT conversion selects original agent_types argmax vehicle0, including ego without ego-mask exclusion. Baseline matched reference mode uses exactly the same4096filenames for both GEN repeats.
metric_definitions.score_units: JSDs are dimensionless natural-log divergence: scipy JensenShannonDistance squared, near/lat *10; angle/length/width/speed *100. Collision is percentage. Physical feature units are not score units.

findings: The frozen combo improves L/W and collision on both completed TRAIN seeds, but speed changes reverse: TRAIN817+10.97%, TRAIN1817+36.39%; the latter violates the predeclared15% speed gate. A lower seven-metric average does not certify eligibility.

Use real speed bins, not an assumed missing-stationary mode. The817 final low-speed[0,1)m/s band is excessive, while high-speed tails are underrepresented. The1817 bands below provide an independent diagnostic rather than extrapolating817's pattern.

Magnitude mismatch is not an unsupervised target here: the7D scalar speed is already directly supervised by normalized MSE. The vector magnitude auxiliary is deliberately disabled/rejected for scalar speed. Adding the same scalar loss again only changes its effective weight.

Loss p is inverse time: clamp(t,.05)^(-p) divided by the uniform-time analytic mean. Higher p emphasizes nearly clean t~0 rather than noisy t~1. Scalar-speed weight4 does not fix source matching or make high-noise transport training distribution-aware.

The frozen combo/control comparison changes batch/update count, ego angle context encoding, shape time powers and speed coefficient together. Equal exposure does not isolate speed weight or context as a causal factor; adaptive EMA effective decay also differs at8192 versus4096 updates. Future ablations must separate these changes.

Scalar-speed decoding along generated heading preserves the norm used by speed JSD. A bad generated heading does not directly alter the decoded speed norm, though shared training/features can correlate their errors.

The x0 MSE conditional mean is theoretically compatible with the correct probability-flow velocity for a linear interpolant under exact learning/integration. Therefore MSE alone does not prove unavoidable marginal collapse. Finite shared capacity, low-time emphasis, discrete sampling, source coupling and generated type selection are plausible interacting causes, not measured causal attribution.

Hungarian matching permutes complete physical source rows within each scene and GT-type group; ego source stays paired to ego. Targets/type labels are not permuted. Normalized seven-coordinate squared costs share an assignment, so position/heading/L/W can overrule speed ordering. Loss coefficient changes do not change this default coupling.

Generated class0 rows define every attribute metric population. Classification error can alter speed/shape marginals without any direct state-coordinate bug. Keep vehicle coverage and per-GT-type supplementary diagnostics alongside the unchanged native metrics.

Linear scalar-speed output is clamped only at final decoding; Gaussian endpoint has about21.6% negative physical source mass from shared TRAINmean/std. This is allowed in the internal interpolant, not evidence that21.6% generated vehicles are stationary. Actual histograms cannot identify preclamp negatives or exactzero mass.

Rare large L/W tails remain sparse even when global shape JSD improves; fixed GT ego dimensions are included in native histograms. Shape JSD improvement can accompany better dominant bins while rarer large vehicles worsen.

The native4096 validation cache/reference alignment is checked here in physical speed/L/W units. No metric/filter definition is altered. Initial-scene velocity is continuous, not decoded motion-token velocity.
